plan.guidance: A protected folder. Prior generated drafts made the lock shackle counter too small and cut an unintended circular notch into the filled lock body. Redesign the composition to leave a generous, readable opening in the shackle at native size. The shackle should meet the lock body cleanly. In filled paint use a coherent lock silhouette cut out of the folder; avoid an isolated black dot or full circle intruding into the body. Keep the folder tab a natural part of its silhouette and preserve the reference family proportions. Use render and lint to inspect the actual result before finishing. This is development feedback, not an accepted reference drawing.

audit.reason: The composition is visually heavy on the left and awkward on the right due to nesting the lock inside an extra cutout frame, which clutters the shape and hurts small-scale legibility.

attempts.condition: 12 admitted Blode components and labelled references; high effort, 24 steps. Plan said 16,384 tokens but CLI actually used 4,096.
attempts.outcome: Both paints ended at length limit; partial shield and incomplete body; rejected.
attempts.lesson: Fix option forwarding. Preserve execution-correction.json; this run cannot test the intended allowance.

plan.guidance: Design folder-lock as a new composition in this family. The folder-shield reference shows how a large, legible badge occupies the lower-right and the folder outline stops around it. Use the admitted curved components where appropriate; avoid redrawing their polished shoulders as overlapping rectangles. The named components identify their intended paint. Do not use outlined parts as filled solids. The shield component itself is not the requested lock. Preserve a generous shackle counter and at least 1 unit of actual white space. Do not squeeze a standalone lock into the folder interior. Do not copy an entire reference icon and rename it. Plan proportions before placing; compare at native size and inspect joins. Reuse of reference components is intentional in this experiment and is not a claim of wholly novel source contours.
